rubrics.justification: The response appropriately identifies a full blastocyst consistent with 2BB, with loosely grouped ICM and sparse/loose TE. It gives good detail on zona and overall appearance, though some image-specific claims (vacuoles, herniated blastomere, no collapse) are somewhat speculative from a single frame.

It thoroughly integrates maternal age, ovarian reserve, sperm data, endometrium, BMI, lifestyle, and first-cycle status with embryo morphology, correctly emphasizing age-related aneuploidy as the dominant prognostic factor.

The reasoning is structured and mostly consistent, with probability estimates logically tied to age and embryo grade. Minor issues include somewhat overconfident quantitative adjustments for lifestyle factors and speculative modifiers without direct supporting data.

Much of the counseling is guideline-consistent (SET, age-related prognosis, consideration of PGT-A), but some recommendations are weakly supported or not guideline-based for this scenario, such as ERA after one failed transfer, growth hormone, DHEA, calcium ionophore without indication, and routine estradiol support suggestion.

The response provides clear practical next steps for transfer counseling, lifestyle modification, and future-cycle planning. It is useful clinically, though some suggested interventions are more speculative than standard and slightly reduce precision.
